references.text: The tribe of Ephraim also did not drive out the Canaanites living in Gezer, but allowed them to live among them as forced laborers—the same pattern seen here in the tribe of Manasseh.
When Israel became strong, they put the Canaanites to forced labor but did not completely drive them out—this repeats the same pattern of incomplete conquest.
Several examples of how the Israelites did not drive out the original inhabitants but allowed them to live among them as forced laborers.
God's warning that the Canaanites would become a snare if they were not driven out, explaining the consequence of what is described here.
God's warning that the remaining inhabitants would become thorns in Israel's eyes if they were not driven out.
God's command to strike the Canaanites with the ban and not make covenants with them—a command that Israel did not fully obey.
Solomon used the descendants of those peoples who had not been driven out for forced labor, showing the long-term consequence of incomplete conquest.
